summary: Elevated TTFB and delayed chat session start after inference optimizer swap for a Dedicated customer
description: Issue summary: BrightHealth AI reports a pronounced increase in time-to-first-token (TTFB) and delayed chat session initiation starting ~2026-03-08 02:15 UTC. The customer observed long initial waits (~1.2-2.5s) for the first token where baseline is ~80-200ms. Impact: Customer-facing chat features experienced user-visible stalls and increased abandonment for peak traffic windows; affects several routes pinned to dedicated pool. Timeline: - 2026-03-07 23:00 UTC: Redwood pushed inference optimizer swap (auto-kernel selector + new batching heuristic) to dedicated pool for BrightHealth. - 2026-03-08 01:40 UTC: BrightHealth reports initial slow sessions. - 2026-03-08 02:00-03:00 UTC: Support started triage. Environment: Dedicated capacity (dedicated pool id dp-0319), prod-us-east, routes: /v1/chat/completions (customer-configured model pin to redwood-7b-quantized-v1). Steps to reproduce: 1) Create chat completion request with system + user prompt (typical size 30-60 tokens). 2) Observe first-byte latency measured at client side. 3) Repeat across a few requests to the same pinned model/route. Observed behavior: First-byte latency spikes on session start and after cache expiry. Warm subsequent tokens are normal. In some cases streaming connection remains open but first token delayed. Expected behavior: First byte emitted within ~100-300ms under dedicated capacity. Logs/Traces: Attached truncated traces and p50/p95 TTFB from customer dashboard and our agent traces. Attachments: brighthealth_ttbf_samples_2026-03-08.csv, trace_dp-0319_2026-03-08.json

Working with runtime eng to add eager kernel pre-touch for dedicated pools and tweak batching heuristic thresholds for session-start windows.

investigation_notes: Findings summary: 1) Kernel initialization (lazy path introduced in runtime PR #4823) is the largest single contributor to elevated TTFB. Measured kernel_init_duration in traces: median ~0.6s, p95 ~1.1s for affected sessions. 2) Scheduler batching behavior at session start produced low-fill micro-batches that increased queuing overhead; this is amplified when kernel_init is non-negligible. 3) KV cache behavior was considered but cache miss penalties were minor (~30-80ms) relative to kernel_init. 4) Routing layer was intermittently directing requests to quantized variant which triggers an extra pre-processing conversion in the compatibility layer adding ~120ms. Experiments run: - Pinned to prior runtime tag rtime-2026-02-28: TTFB returned to baseline. - Forced eager kernel pre-touch on one node in canary pool: initial token latency reduced by ~700ms on canary. Hypothesis: combining eager pre-touch with improved early batching heuristics will restore baseline TTFB without disabling optimizer features. Next steps: merge hotfix PR #5078, run canary for 24h, monitor kernel_init_duration and p95 TTFB, and then perform staged rollout to dedicated pools. Linked runbook: confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/post-deploy-latency-checklist
workaround: Customer workaround validated: pin the route to rtime-2026-02-28 (previous runtime) which bypasses the lazy-kernel path. Steps provided to customer: update route config in Console > Routes > [route] > Runtime Tag = rtime-2026-02-28, then restart route. This reduces TTFB to baseline while fix is prepared.
resolution: In progress: hotfix PR #5078 (eager pre-warm on session allocation + scheduler threshold adjustment) created and under QA. Customer verified workaround (runtime pin) and will wait for hotfix rollout. After canary validation, plan is staged rollout to dedicated pools. Post-rollback action: add kernel_init_duration to per-pool dashboards and create alert on p95 > 500ms.
customer_notes: BrightHealth engineers provided additional traces and said the issue surfaced during their morning peak. They are sensitive to any regressions during business hours and requested a fix that does not require long maintenance windows.
postmortem_followup_tasks: Add automated canary for runtime optimizer swaps
Document runtime-tag rollback procedure in customer runbook
